items.stem: Define the term “the law of independent assortment”.
items.answer: The law that in inheritance of two pairs of traits the segregation of one pair is independent of the other.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the law that in inheritance of two pairs of traits the segregation of one pair is independent of the other.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Mendel's laws and crosses is correct?
items.answer: Mendel worked on garden pea for seven years (1856–1863).
items.markingKey: (a) Mendel worked on garden pea for seven years (1856–1863). The other statements are false. It is 1 : 2 : 1; the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1. It is based on the dihybrid cross. He studied 7 pairs (14 true-breeding varieties).
options: Mendel worked on garden pea for seven years (1856–1863).
The monohybrid F₂ genotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
The law of independent assortment is based on the monohybrid cross.
Mendel studied 14 pairs of contrasting traits in pea.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Mendel worked on garden pea for seven years (1856–1863).
Reason (R): The law of independent assortment is based on the monohybrid cross.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It is based on the dihybrid cross.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The law of independent assortment is based on the monohybrid cross.”
items.answer: It is based on the dihybrid cross.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It is based on the dihybrid cross.

items.stem: In pea plants, yellow seeds (Y) is dominant over green seeds (y). What is the phenotypic ratio of the progeny of the cross Yy × Yy?
items.answer: 3 yellow seeds : 1 green seeds
items.markingKey: (a) Gametes combine to give 1 YY : 2 Yy : 1 yy, i.e. 3 yellow seeds : 1 green seeds.
options: 3 yellow seeds : 1 green seeds
all green seeds
all yellow seeds
1 yellow seeds : 1 green seeds

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Mendel's laws and crosses is incorrect?
items.answer: The monohybrid F₂ genotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “The monohybrid F₂ genotypic ratio is 3 : 1.” Correct form: It is 1 : 2 : 1; the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
options: The dihybrid F₂ phenotypic ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
The monohybrid F₂ genotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
A test cross with a heterozygote gives a 1 : 1 ratio.
The monohybrid F₂ phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1 and genotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.

items.stem:
Arnav, a student in Bhopal, crosses a pure tall pea plant with a pure dwarf one. All F₁ plants are tall. He selfs the F₁ and raises 800 F₂ plants.
(i) How many F₂ plants are expected to be dwarf? (1 mark)
(ii) Which law explains the reappearance of dwarf plants? (1 mark)
(iii) How would he find out whether a tall F₂ plant is TT or Tt? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) 200 (¼ of 800). (ii) Law of segregation. (iii) Test cross with a dwarf (tt) plant: all tall progeny ⇒ TT; tall and dwarf in 1 : 1 ⇒ Tt.

items.stem: In pea, round seeds (R) is dominant over wrinkled seeds (r) and axial flowers (A) is dominant over terminal flowers (a); the genes assort independently. A plant RrAa is selfed and 800 seeds are raised. What fraction of the progeny, and how many plants, are expected to show round seeds and terminal flowers?
items.answer: 3/16; 150 plants
items.markingKey: Each gene segregates 3 : 1 (or 1 : 2 : 1 for genotype) independently (1); probability = 3/16 (1); 3/16 × 800 = 150 plants (1).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The monohybrid F₂ genotypic ratio is 3 : 1.”
items.answer: It is 1 : 2 : 1; the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It is 1 : 2 : 1; the phenotypic ratio is 3 : 1.

items.stem: Explain the term “the law of independent assortment”.
items.answer: The law that in inheritance of two pairs of traits the segregation of one pair is independent of the other.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the law that in inheritance of two pairs of traits the segregation of one pair is independent of the other.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The recessive trait reappears in the F₂ generation.
Reason (R): Alleles do not blend in the F₁ hybrid.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Law of segregation.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Mehak crosses a yellow seeds pea plant of unknown genotype with a green seeds plant (yy) and gets all 120 yellow seeds plants. What is this cross called, and what is the genotype of the yellow seeds parent?
items.answer: Test cross; YY (homozygous)
items.markingKey: Crossing with the recessive parent is a test cross (1); no green seeds progeny appear, so the yellow seeds parent gives only Y gametes ⇒ YY (homozygous) (1).

items.stem: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). What is the phenotypic ratio of the progeny of the cross Tt × Tt?
items.answer: 3 tall : 1 dwarf
items.markingKey: (c) Gametes combine to give 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, i.e. 3 tall : 1 dwarf.
options: all dwarf
1 tall : 1 dwarf
3 tall : 1 dwarf
all tall

items.stem: Explain the term “polygenic inheritance”.
items.answer: Inheritance in which a trait is controlled by three or more genes, each with an additive effect, as in human skin colour.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inheritance in which a trait is controlled by three or more genes, each with an additive effect, as in human skin colour.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about deviations from Mendelism is correct?
items.answer: In incomplete dominance the F₂ phenotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.
items.markingKey: (a) In incomplete dominance the F₂ phenotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1. The other statements are false. AB blood group has the genotype IᴬIᴮ. There are six genotypes and four phenotypes. That is polygenic inheritance; pleiotropy is one gene affecting many traits.
options: In incomplete dominance the F₂ phenotypic ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.
A person with blood group AB has the genotype IᴬI°.
There are four genotypes for the ABO blood group.
Pleiotropy means a single trait is controlled by many genes.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): ABO blood group alleles Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant.
Reason (R): Pleiotropy means a single trait is controlled by many genes.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: That is polygenic inheritance; pleiotropy is one gene affecting many traits.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.answer: That is polygenic inheritance; pleiotropy is one gene affecting many traits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: That is polygenic inheritance; pleiotropy is one gene affecting many traits.

items.stem: ABO blood groups are controlled by gene I with alleles Iᴬ, Iᴮ (co-dominant) and I° (recessive). What blood groups, and in what proportions, are expected among children of parents IᴬIᴬ × IᴬI°?
items.answer: A only
items.markingKey: (d) Gametes Iᴬ, Iᴬ × Iᴬ, I° give A only.
options: AB only
O only
B only
A only

items.stem:
Kiran crosses a red-flowered snapdragon with a white-flowered one. All F₁ plants have pink flowers. She selfs the F₁.
(i) Name the type of inheritance. (1 mark)
(ii) Give the F₂ phenotypic and genotypic ratios. (2 marks)
(iii) Why does this not disprove Mendel's law of segregation? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Incomplete dominance. (ii) Phenotype 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white; genotype 1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr. (iii) The parental red and white phenotypes reappear in F₂, showing that alleles did not blend but segregated.

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of incomplete dominance?
items.answer: starch grain size in pea
items.markingKey: (a) Starch grain size in pea is an example of incomplete dominance; the others are not.
options: starch grain size in pea
human height
human skin colour
phenylketonuria in humans

items.stem: A child has blood group O. If the father has blood group A and the mother blood group B, work out the genotypes of the parents and the possible genotypes of the other offspring.
items.answer: Father IᴬI°, mother IᴮI°. Offspring: IᴬIᴮ (AB), IᴬI° (A), IᴮI° (B), I°I° (O), each ¼.
items.markingKey: 1 mark parents; 1 mark offspring.

items.stem: ABO blood groups are controlled by gene I with alleles Iᴬ, Iᴮ (co-dominant) and I° (recessive). What blood groups, and in what proportions, are expected among children of parents IᴬI° × IᴬIᴮ?
items.markingKey: (d) Gametes Iᴬ, I° × Iᴬ, Iᴮ give A (1/2), B (1/4), AB (1/4).

items.stem: Which term describes inheritance in which both alleles express themselves fully in the F₁, as in AB blood group?
items.answer: co-dominance
items.markingKey: (c) Co-dominance: inheritance in which both alleles express themselves fully in the F₁, as in AB blood group.
options: incomplete dominance
polygenic inheritance
co-dominance

Human skin colour is an example of polygenic inheritance.

items.stem: What is meant by “linkage”?
items.answer: The physical association of genes on a chromosome.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the physical association of genes on a chromosome.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about chromosomal theory, linkage and sex determination is correct?
items.answer: Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes.
items.markingKey: (a) Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes. The other statements are false. Tightly linked genes show very low recombination; loosely linked genes show higher recombination. In birds females are ZW (heterogametic) and males ZZ. The father's sperm carries X or Y and decides the sex.
options: Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes.
Tightly linked genes show high recombination.
In humans the mother decides the sex of the child.
In birds the male is heterogametic.

Assertion (A): Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes.

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: What type of sex determination is found in honey bee?
items.answer: haplodiploidy
items.markingKey: (a) Honey bee: haplodiploidy; males develop from unfertilised eggs (haploid) and females from fertilised eggs (diploid).
options: haplodiploidy
ZW–ZZ (female heterogamety)
XX–XY (male heterogamety)
XX–XO (male heterogamety)

Mendel discovered linkage in pea.
Alfred Sturtevant used recombination frequency to map genes on chromosomes.
In birds the female is heterogametic (ZW).

items.stem:
A poultry farmer near Namakkal wants to know which parent decides the sex of chicks.
(i) What are the sex chromosomes of a hen and a cock? (1 mark)
(ii) Which parent decides the sex of the chick? (1 mark)
(iii) How is this different from humans? Explain with gametes. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Hen ZW, cock ZZ. (ii) The hen, as she produces Z and W eggs. (iii) In humans the male is heterogametic (XY) and produces X and Y sperms; the female (XX) produces only X eggs, so the father decides.

items.stem: In Morgan's dihybrid crosses in Drosophila, why were the F₂ ratios very different from 9 : 3 : 3 : 1?
items.answer: The two genes were on the X chromosome (linked), so parental combinations were much more frequent than recombinants; the proportion of recombinants depended on the distance between the genes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark linkage; 1 mark recombination/distance.

items.stem: Which term describes the structure seen by Henking in some insect sperms, later named the X chromosome?
items.answer: the X body
items.markingKey: (c) The X body: the structure seen by Henking in some insect sperms, later named the X chromosome.
options: male heterogamety
recombination
the X body
female heterogamety

items.stem: In a test cross of Drosophila involving the linked genes yellow body (y) and vermilion eye (v), 100 of 1000 progeny were recombinants. Calculate the recombination frequency and the map distance between the genes.
items.answer: 10%; 10 map units (cM)
items.markingKey: Recombination frequency = recombinants/total × 100 = 100/1000 × 100 = 10% (1); 1% recombination = 1 map unit, so distance = 10 cM (1).

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In humans the mother decides the sex of the child.”
items.answer: The father's sperm carries X or Y and decides the sex.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The father's sperm carries X or Y and decides the sex.

options: XX–XO (male heterogamety)

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Drosophila is a good material for genetic studies.
Reason (R): It completes its life cycle in about two weeks and a single mating gives a large number of progeny.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Also easy to grow and has clear hereditary variations.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Describe the different mechanisms of sex determination with examples: XX–XY, XX–XO, ZW–ZZ and haplodiploidy.
items.answer: XX–XY: humans, Drosophila; male XY produces X and Y sperms (male heterogamety). XX–XO: grasshopper; male has one X, produces sperm with and without X. ZW–ZZ: birds; female ZW is heterogametic. Haplodiploidy: honey bee; fertilised eggs (2n = 32) become females, unfertilised (n = 16) become males by parthenogenesis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each system; 1 mark heterogamety concept.

items.stem: Define the term “a frameshift mutation”.
items.answer: A mutation caused by insertion or deletion of base pairs that shifts the reading frame.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a mutation caused by insertion or deletion of base pairs that shifts the reading frame.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disorder due to sex-chromosome aneuploidy or X-linked recessive disorder: Klinefelter's syndrome, colour blindness, haemophilia.
items.answer: Klinefelter's syndrome – disorder due to sex-chromosome aneuploidy; colour blindness – X-linked recessive disorder; haemophilia – X-linked recessive disorder.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Klinefelter's syndrome – disorder due to sex-chromosome aneuploidy; colour blindness – X-linked recessive disorder; haemophilia – X-linked recessive disorder.

items.stem:
In a family in Hyderabad, both parents are normal, but their son suffers from a disorder in which his blood does not clot properly. His sister is normal.
(i) Name the disorder and how it is inherited. (1 mark)
(ii) Write the genotypes of the parents. (2 marks)
(iii) What is the chance that the sister is a carrier? (1 mark)
items.answer: (i) Haemophilia; X-linked recessive. (ii) Mother XᴴXʰ (carrier), father XᴴY (normal). (iii) ½ (50%).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Klinefelter's syndrome and Down's syndrome on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A genetic disorder shows these features: individuals are sterile. Identify the disorder – Klinefelter's syndrome or Down's syndrome? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Klinefelter's syndrome: karyotype 47, XXY; overall masculine development; gynaecomastia (breast development). Down's syndrome: trisomy of chromosome 21; short stature with small round head; furrowed tongue and partially open mouth. (b) Klinefelter's syndrome.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Klinefelter's syndrome; 1 mark: “individuals are sterile” is a feature of Klinefelter's syndrome.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about mutation, pedigree analysis and genetic disorders is correct?

items.stem: In a test cross of Drosophila involving the linked genes cut wing (ct) and white eye (w), 10 of 800 progeny were recombinants. Calculate the recombination frequency and the map distance between the genes.
items.answer: 1.25%; 1.25 map units (cM)
